title: Optimize a Slow Database View
prompt:
Measure query behavior, inspect generated SQL, identify repeated related-object lookups, and compare before/after results.

Submission: a small reviewable artifact, relevant tests, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/environment notes. Use synthetic data. Django/Python server code is not executed by CodeLeaf browser preview; local or human review is required.
target_skills: Establish a reproducible baseline with representative data.
Use query inspection and appropriate relation loading.
Report both correctness and measured performance differences.

starter.content:
books = Book.objects.select_related("author").order_by("title")
for book in books:
    print(book.title, book.author.name)
# Compare with/without select_related using query capture.

expected_output: Query count matters but is not identical to response latency; include repeatable measurements.
acceptance_criteria: Optimized output matches the reference result.
Performance claims include environment and data assumptions.
State whether verification was local, static, or human-reviewed.
Do not claim a build/deployment or external integration was tested unless it was actually run.
hints: Avoid guessing at an index before inspecting query plans.
Check N+1 related-object access in templates and serializers.
Use an index only when the workload supports it.
grading_method: Required-string smoke check plus human review of technical correctness, tests, safe handling, expected result and reproducibility. This does not execute arbitrary Python/Django code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend owns its uniform XP/idempotency rules.
